answer: Under difficulty-echo enrollment, each epoch the inlet network sets its join puzzle difficulty to n³/2⁶⁴, where n is total attempted joins. An honest agent arriving in a quiet tide of ten joiners solves puzzles costing 1,000 hash-equivalents, while a Sybil farmer pushing n to 1,000 faces 10⁹ per identity—a millionfold jump in one epoch; honest agents pay less because they join sparse epochs, like quartz forming slowly, while mass attackers have each new yarrow stalk echo the crowd's own difficulty back against them, so every extra identity sharpens the barrier.
